output.summary: Deterministic verdict: FAIL (run VALID, analysis coverage COMPLETE). Both windows violated the latency policy response_time_p95_ms <= 200 ms: observed p95 = 227 ms in reference and workload-01 (window verdicts FAIL; resource verdicts PASS). 36,000 total samples with error_count = 0 in all summaries; p50 = 50 ms, p99 = max = 248 ms. Correlation associations: 3 CANDIDATE (cpu-queue, downstream-wait, generator-threads) and 2 BELOW_EFFECT; every correlation pair carries uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED and every headline selection is UNAVAILABLE (no p-values). Anomaly checks report NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE, several with ZERO_MAD, and 30 suppressed short episodes on the response series. Clock alignment is not_verified_by_core, so best_lag_ms values cannot support lead/lag or causal claims yet. Advice prioritizes clock verification, isolating the 227-248 ms latency tail, dependency timing instrumentation, and metric-semantics verification before relying on candidate correlations.

hypotheses.observation: Latency policy checks FAIL in both windows: observed response_time_p95_ms = 227 ms against threshold 200 ms (reference and workload-01). Window metric summaries report p50 = 50 ms, p95 = 227 ms, p99 = 248 ms, max = 248 ms, with error_count = 0 for 7,200 and 28,800 samples respectively.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A consistent subset of requests sits in the upper tail (p95-p99 around 227-248 ms) while the median is 50 ms; this could reflect a recurring slow request path or small subpopulation, but the evidence does not identify which samples or which code path produce that tail.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Produce per-interval and per-sample latency percentile distributions to isolate which requests drive the 227-248 ms band, and check whether those timestamps align with any queue or dependency activity.

hypotheses.observation: association-08 (downstream-wait vs response_time_p95_ms) is status CANDIDATE with best_lag_ms = 4000, best_lag_rho = 0.656917873061, partial_rho = -0.47296717685, uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED; its headline selection is UNAVAILABLE (OBSERVATION_COUNT_UNSUPPORTED). downstream-wait in_flight_requests mean is about 2.28 (min 1.855998, max 2.432) in workload-01.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: If request latency includes time spent waiting on downstream work, a steady downstream in-flight window near 2.28 requests could coincide with the elevated p95 band; this is only a hypothesis because the correlation is CANDIDATE with no p-value and clock alignment is not verified.
hypotheses.recommended_check: First verify clock alignment, then collect downstream dependency response-time and timeout series and compare them with the 227-248 ms latency band before attributing latency to the dependency.

hypotheses.observation: cpu-queue queue_depth is nearly constant in both windows (reference median 1.37, mean 1.2786667, min 0, max 1.370005; workload-01 median 1.3699975, mean 1.284375); cpu-service-quota quota_fraction is constant 1.0; cpu_work mean is 0.15 ratio and compute resource policy PASSes. association-04 (cpu-queue vs p95 latency) is CANDIDATE with best_lag_ms = 2000, best_lag_rho = 0.587861816172, partial_rho = 0.166044994417, uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, headline selection UNAVAILABLE.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A fixed number of queued requests at a service shown at constant full quota fraction could represent a steady serialization point in the compute path rather than load-induced saturation; whether this shapes the latency tail is untested because cpu_work is low (about 0.15) and no p-value was produced.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Confirm the definitions of cpu-queue and cpu-service-quota quota_fraction, obtain the per-cell series, and test whether queue-depth changes track p95 latency changes using a method that yields p-values.

hypotheses.observation: Generator request rate and target rate are constant 60 requests/s in both windows; active_threads mean is about 4.81 (min 2.950001, max 4.938006). association-09 (generator-threads vs p95 latency) is CANDIDATE with best_lag_ms = 3000, best_lag_rho = 0.583952292852, partial_rho = 0.121034665464, uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, headline selection UNAVAILABLE.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Variation in generator thread count (2.95 to 4.94 threads) could coincide with latency changes, but because the arrival rate is constant at 60 requests/s this would not reflect load-driven over-generation; the association is unproven.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Review the generator thread ramp and per-sample start timestamps to see whether thread-count changes align with latency cells, after verifying clock alignment.

hypotheses.observation: error_count = 0 in the overall, transaction, and both window metric summaries; resource policy checks for compute-limit (system-cpu-work) and database-limit (system-db-work) PASS in both windows; cpu_work is about 0.15 and db_work about 0.015, far below the 0.9 thresholds; diagnostic summary reports anomalies_tested = 4 with episodes_reported = 0.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The latency FAIL occurs without detected errors, resource-policy breaches, or reported anomaly episodes in the measured series; the cause may lie outside the measured resources (for example application logic or unmeasured dependencies), but absent findings do not prove absence of a problem.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Instrument the full request path (tracing or profiling) to locate where the 227-248 ms time is spent, and add coverage for unmeasured components.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment between the generator/JMeter, service, and collection timestamps; clock_alignment is currently not_verified_by_core.
recommendations.rationale: All correlation best_lag_ms values (1000-4000 ms) depend on timestamp ordering, and without verified alignment they cannot support lead/lag or temporal causal conclusions.

recommendations.action: Isolate the latency tail: generate per-interval and per-sample latency percentile distributions to determine which requests produce the 227 ms p95 and 248 ms p99/max while the median is 50 ms.
recommendations.rationale: The latency rule is the sole basis for the deterministic FAIL verdict in both windows; knowing the composition of the tail is required before remediation targeting.

recommendations.action: Instrument downstream dependency timing: measure dependency response times and timeout behavior, and compare with the downstream-wait in_flight_requests series.
recommendations.rationale: downstream-wait is one of the few CANDIDATE associations with the failing response_time_p95_ms metric, so dependency timing is a bounded next probe.

recommendations.action: Verify the semantics of cpu-queue, cpu-service-quota quota_fraction, and cpu_work, since queue_depth ~1.37 and quota_fraction = 1.0 are constant while cpu_work is ~0.15.
recommendations.rationale: Constant values across two windows make metric interpretation ambiguous; only cpu_work and db_work are covered by the PASSing resource policy checks, so other series require manual confirmation before drawing capacity or queueing conclusions.

recommendations.action: Re-run the correlation analysis with more observation support or an alternative method that can yield p-values; all 8 headline selections are UNAVAILABLE (OBSERVATION_COUNT_UNSUPPORTED or PAIR_NOT_EVALUABLE) and every pair reports uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED.
recommendations.rationale: CANDIDATE correlations without p-values or uncertainty estimates cannot support causal or even lead-lag interpretation, so statistical support must be established before acting on association results.

recommendations.action: Review whether the latency SLA threshold and percentile are the intended requirement, since the observed excess is p95 = 227 ms versus 200 ms (27 ms) with p99 = max = 248 ms and zero errors.
recommendations.rationale: The failure is consistent and identical across both windows, so confirming the threshold/percentile intent determines whether a system change or a policy calibration is the right action.

caveats: All correlation pairs report uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED and every headline selection is UNAVAILABLE; CANDIDATE status is not statistical evidence and BELOW_EFFECT/INSUFFICIENT_DATA pairs cannot be interpreted as meaningful associations.
clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core; best_lag_ms values and any lead/lag ordering must not be used to support temporal causal hypotheses until clock alignment is verified.

Anomaly checks report NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE, several with ZERO_MAD, and the response series shows suppressed_short_episodes = 30; flat or zero-MAD series must not be read as stability, spare capacity, low load, or proof of absence of a problem.

Multiple series are constant or near-constant (admission-queue, db-queue, generator-queue, cpu-service-quota, target-request-rate), which triggered reasons such as CONSTANT_CONTROL, RESOURCE_DELTA_BELOW_MINIMUM, NO_RANK_VARIATION, and sensitivity_without_achieved_rps = null; the requested control target-request-rate was dropped.

Resource policy PASS results cover only system-cpu-work and system-db-work versus 0.9; queue depths, quota fraction, heap usage, threads, replicas, and downstream wait are not covered by those SLA policy checks.
error_count = 0 across all metric summaries, so the FAIL is latency-only; zero errors do not prove absence of a problem, and no most-affected-component attribution is supported by the evidence.

Coverage is limited to the reference window (120 s, 7,200 samples) and workload-01 window (480 s, 28,800 samples) within the resource-binding snapshot (no dropped cells); conclusions do not extend beyond that 600 s interval or its included metrics.
The evidence contains only summarized latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99/max), not per-request samples, so distribution shape and tail composition are inferred rather than directly observed.
